statements.text: Back pain began 07/28/2026 after a fall from standing height, 9 weeks before this visit.

Focal kyphotic deformity at T12 measuring 24 degrees.

Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis.

Primary Care Progress Note
Date: 08/03/2026
Patient: Natalie Boehm, 83-year-old female

Subjective:
Ms. Boehm presents for her routine follow-up visit. She reports feeling generally well with no new complaints. She denies any recent falls, dizziness, or changes in mobility.

Objective:
Vital signs are stable. Physical examination reveals no acute distress. Cardiovascular, respiratory, and abdominal exams are unremarkable. Musculoskeletal exam shows normal range of motion without tenderness or deformity.

Assessment:
Ms. Boehm is an elderly female with stable health status. No new issues identified at this visit.

Plan:
Continue current medications and lifestyle. Encourage regular physical activity and balanced nutrition. Follow up in 6 months or sooner if any concerns arise.

Radiology Report
Date: 09/16/2026
Patient: Natalie Boehm, 83-year-old female

MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/16/2026: acute osteoporotic T12 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging. Interval increase in T12 vertebral body height loss compared with radiographs from 08/01/2026. Focal kyphotic deformity at T12 measuring 24 degrees.

Impression:
There is an acute osteoporotic compression fracture at T12 with bone marrow edema. Interval increase in T12 vertebral body height loss compared with radiographs from 08/01/2026. Focal kyphotic deformity at T12 measuring 24 degrees is present.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is recommended. Follow-up imaging may be considered to assess fracture healing and deformity progression.

Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/28/2026
Patient: Natalie Boehm, 83-year-old female

History:
Back pain began 07/28/2026 after a fall from standing height, 9 weeks before this visit. Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture. Pain NRS 5/10 despite 8 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with acetaminophen and tramadol, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has been stable to slightly improved since the fracture.

Assessment:
Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis. Roland Morris Disability Questionnaire score 21/24.

Plan:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program. Continue current pain management and brace use. Monitor symptoms and functional status closely. Consider further intervention if pain worsens or functional decline occurs.
